correctness.rationale: Exact hyperbolic decomposition of every symmetric positive seasonal exponential, matrix-commutator factorization for all four labels, 3 dihedral order classes, and Perron monotonicity at constant positive determinant prove the universal inequality. Independent rational arithmetic within the bundled verifier checks sample algebra and uses a proved Taylor tail to certify one persistence/decay sign crossing. Does not assert nonlinear population persistence or more than four phases.

A broader unknown four-factor matrix inequality would dominate the claim and remains a stated risk.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Using a prior growth criterion with explicit monodromy does not automatically imply a ratio-only maximizer, strict ordering and opposite-sign witness. Prior two-season persistence mechanisms are respected, not re-asserted as novel. The inaccessible full text of the follow-up is a genuine unresolved publication-priority risk.

The four-season all-permutation ordering and certified opposite-sign growth for fixed environments are stronger than that known invariance. No accessed equivalent statement was identified, but the possibility of an unindexed trace rearrangement remains.

Full primary-source comparisons and direct searches found no covering exact all-four-season contrast order or fixed-season sign-crossing theorem; the algebraic differences are not implied by the inspected two-letter matrix-word and general growth-threshold statements. value.rationale: With four fixed seasonal habitats and positive phasewise symmetric exchange, deciding the best of 24 possible calendar orders is a concrete ecological scheduling problem. The theorem solves it symbolically from four contrast-to-dispersal ratios, proves three or fewer seasons are order-insensitive, and exhibits opposite population growth signs from reordering the same four sink seasons. This is a structural full classification with a consequential sharp boundary, not a numerical or arbitrary slice.
